newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Two Russian soldiers confess to double murder.
newsitem.headline: Two Russian soldiers confess to double murder.

text.p: Two Russian army deserters were detained by police and confessed on Saturday to killing the parents-in-law of a doctor who treats President Boris Yeltsin, Itar-Tass news agency said.

Their confession appeared to be the latest blow to the reputation of the demoralised and underfunded armed forces. Security forces were also hunting two soldiers following the murder of four of their comrades in Russia's far east.
Tass said the police, acting on a tip-off, had found the two deserters in the northwestern region of Karelia carrying documents and other goods belonging to Andrei and Anna Ichko.
ORT television, which is partly owned by the government, identified the Ichkos as the parents-in-law of Vladlen Vtorushin, who has been treating Yeltsin for two years.
Andrei Ichko was found dead with a skull fracture on Wednesday in the stairwell of his Moscow apartment block.

The two deserters confessed to killing him with a metal rod and taking his keys off him. They then entered his apartment and stabbed his wife with the kitchen knife, Tass quoted a police spokesman as saying.
They then fled in their victims' clothes and with their passports and other items, the spokesman said.
Yeltsin, 65, is in a sanatorium outside Moscow waiting to have a heart operation, probably in the next two months.
On the far eastern island of Sakhalin, army troops and elite police were still searching for two soldiers after four of their colleagues in an air defence unit were shot dead on Thursday.
Tass said one of the men had suddenly opened fire, killing a warrant officer and three soldiers, and both had then fled.
The shooting overshadowed a tour of the far east by Defence Minister Igor Rodionov, but the minister said on Saturday he was generally pleased with his visit.

"On the whole I am satisfied with the state of affairs in the far east. The morale in the (military) district, the navy and the region is normal, making it possible for difficulties to be overcome," Tass quoted him as saying.
"The far eastern troops need only to be given some assistance. I think this assistance will be offered after I make my report to the government and the Russian president."
The far east, including Vladivostok which is home to the Pacific fleet, has been badly hit by financial problems besetting the armed forces and other sectors of the economy.
Yeltsin has expressed concern at the state of the armed forces and security chief Alexander Lebed has said they could soon mutiny.
Rodionov says he rules out a mutiny. He hopes the government will revise its draft budget for 1997, rejected at the first reading on Friday, to increase defence spending.
